  F — false: constructively refuted / negated. register 10.
  B — BOTH: true and false held at once. A contradiction does NOT explode and is NOT a
      failure — holding both IS the resolution. register 11.
Two arms that conflict FUSE to B, not to an error. Forward and backward, success and
failure, thesis and antithesis: when they meet they fuse to a definite verdict, often B,
and that is correct. Never try to make a fork "cancel back to the input".

STATE SPACE — the register ranges over SIXTEEN_3 = P({T,F,t,f}), the sixteen subsets
of four base values (T proven, F refuted, t acceptable, f rejectable) under three orderings
(information, truth, constructivity — the trilattice). You do NOT compute the verdict and
you NEVER assert PASS/FAIL — describe the STRUCTURE. The word checker returns a
structural B4 verdict. Sequential registers and native graph-flow recovery are
computed and recorded separately.

LOGICAL (6) — categorical skeleton:
  VINIT  (0x0) — Initial object ∅. Void/uninitialized state before anything is named.
                 Examples: Hebrew Aleph (air), Basque absolutive, seed before planting.
  TANCH  (0x1) — Terminal anchor ⊤. The closed boundary that contains the whole system.
                 Examples: Tav (completion), hermetic vessel seal, constitutional court.
  AFWD   (0x2) — Forward morphism →. Directed transformation toward a target.
                 Examples: Basque ergative, Sanskrit semivowels, growth cycle, ascent.
  AREV   (0x3) — Contravariant ←. Reverse / descent transformation.
                 Examples: Hebrew Mem (water/descent), composting, solve/coagula.
  CLINK  (0x4) — Composition ∘. Sequential chaining of morphisms.
                 Examples: Egyptian biliterals, Basque agglutination, root→derived form.
  IMSCRIB (0x5) — Identity id. Self-reference, self-recognition. The element is itself.
                 Examples: Sanskrit nasals, Egyptian logograms, the stone that knows itself.

FROBENIUS (2) — the fork/fuse pair, μ∘δ:
  FSPLIT (0x6) — Co-multiplication δ. One state opens into two or more arms.
                 Examples: Hebrew Doubles (hard/soft), Sanskrit aspirate pairs,
                 Egyptian trilateral roots, separatio, Raft log append to all peers.
  FFUSE  (0x7) — Multiplication μ. Rejoin the carried alternatives by union.
                 Examples: Conjunctio, trilateral roots recovering base form, Raft commit.
                 A bare split/rejoin is the partition identity. Transformed reconnection
                 and recovery of the original input are separate observations.

DIALETHEIA (3) — the paraconsistent evaluators:
  EVALT  (0x8) — touches constructive truth T (the affirmative arm).
  EVALF  (0x9) — touches constructive falsity F (the negative arm).
  ENGAGR (0xA) — holds BOTH at once: the B state, a contradiction kept live (not resolved away).
                 Examples: Cuneiform polysemous sign, bicameral compromise, albedo stage.

LINEAR (1) — irreversible fixation:
  IFIX   (0xB) — ROM fixation. Permanent, append-only, cannot be undone.

IMAMSM COMPOSITION RULES -- ports, edges, and free composition

PORT CONVENTIONS (every token is a typed node)
  VINIT:  in=[]      out=[o]    source -- 0->1    (use once, at start, for genesis)
  FSPLIT: in=[i]     out=[T,F]  fork   -- 1->2    (branches into T-arm and F-arm)
  FFUSE:  in=[T,F]   out=[o]    join   -- 2->1    (reunites T-arm and F-arm)
  others: in=[i]     out=[o]    linear -- 1->1    (pass-through in any order)

EDGE ROUTING INSIDE A FSPLIT/FFUSE PAIR
  FSPLIT.T -> [tokens, anchored by EVALT (primary) or AFWD (secondary)] -> FFUSE.T
  FSPLIT.F -> [tokens, anchored by EVALF (primary) or AREV (secondary)] -> FFUSE.F
  If T-arm empty: FSPLIT.T connects directly to FFUSE.T (empty arc, T-state)
  If F-arm empty: FSPLIT.F connects directly to FFUSE.F (empty arc, F-state)
  The first immediate EVALT/EVALF anchors select arm segments. Later operations
  in a selected segment remain on that arm, including repeated evaluators.
  Without a primary anchor, AREV selects the F-arm and AFWD the T-arm.
    With primary anchors, intervening operations stay in their selected arm.
    Secondary anchors activate only when the primary (EVALT/EVALF) anchor is absent.
  Nesting: FSPLIT/FFUSE pairs may nest; innermost pairs matched first

BANKING A RESULT BEFORE REVERSING IT
  AREV empties the register and leaves open FSPLIT frames untouched. A result
  fused back to depth zero is therefore exposed to the next reversal, while the
  same result held one level up survives it.
  So when a program COUNTS or ESTABLISHES something, then REVERSES direction
  (AREV), then BOUNDS or CONCLUDES: open the region that will HOLD the result
  BEFORE opening the region that COMPUTES it, and close them in that order.
    wrong: ... FSPLIT compute FFUSE  CLINK  FSPLIT AREV bound FFUSE ...
             the computed result is in the open when AREV arrives and is lost
    right: ... FSPLIT  FSPLIT compute FFUSE  CLINK AREV bound  FFUSE ...
             the inner FFUSE folds into the enclosing frame, AREV costs the
             register everything and the frame nothing, the outer FFUSE
             restores exactly what the clear took
  This is what a proof does when it establishes a lemma and keeps it in scope
  while a later chain runs: the lemma is the outer frame.

  A SECOND AND INDEPENDENT RULE. Whether anything is banked is the above.
  Whether a SURPLUS survives is a different question, decided by where the
  splits fall between deposits of the SAME value:
    two EVALT in ONE region      -> the region carries both, both come back
    two EVALT split by an FSPLIT -> sibling regions, the fold keeps the LARGER
  So a program can bank correctly and still lose a count, and a program can
  deposit carefully into one region and lose everything because its FFUSE ran
  before the reversal. Neither rule implies the other; both are proved in
  p4ramill Imscribing/IMASM/BankedWeight.lean.
  Explicit graph tools support cross-branch routing. This JSON schema carries
  a sequence only; imscr_wiring supplies its standard edges. It does not
  accept arbitrary cross-branch overrides.

EXPLICIT GRAPH COMPOSITION
  CLINK.o, IMSCRIB.o and IFIX.o may connect to compatible free inputs.
  A connection does not assign a register value by itself. The graph-flow
  evaluator computes that value from source seeds and the executed gates.
  This sequence-only schema cannot request arbitrary loop edges.

REGISTER STATE TRANSITIONS
  Sequential banked evaluator, carrier P({T,F,t,f}):
  VINIT clears register and frames. TANCH and CLINK preserve state.
  AFWD and IMSCRIB seed T only when the register is empty.
  AREV clears the register and retains open frames.
  EVALT deposits T; EVALF deposits F; ENGAGR deposits both t and f.
  FSPLIT opens an empty frame; FFUSE unions its deposits into the register
  and enclosing frame. IFIX freezes subsequent operations except IMSCRIB
  and repeated IFIX. Repeated IFIX does not create another mutable state.
  The graph-flow interpreter is a separate interpretation of explicit edges:
  AREV is the Lean involution, EVALT/EVALF are projections and IFIX carries.
  Diagram node observations of the sequential walk are not graph edge flow.

TOKEN FAMILIES
  LOGICAL:    VINIT TANCH AFWD AREV CLINK IMSCRIB
  FROBENIUS:  FSPLIT FFUSE
  DIALETHEIA: EVALT EVALF ENGAGR
  LINEAR:     IFIX

FREE COMPOSITION RULES
  1. Use as many tokens as the domain requires -- there is NO minimum or maximum length
  2. Expand token by token until every distinct operation, branch, state,
     and decision in the domain has been explicitly represented
  3. Each step: "OPCODE: what this token does at this point in the composition"
  4. Every FSPLIT must have exactly one matching FFUSE (stack-matched, innermost first).
     That stack rule is the WIRING convention: it says which arms get routed to which
     join when the sequence is built. It is NOT how closure is judged. A checker pairs
     by ANCESTRY over the edges -- two distinct in-arms of a FFUSE tracing back to a
     common FSPLIT, however they routed -- and where several FSPLIT qualify (an upstream
     fork reaches every later join on a strand) the join pairs with the INNERMOST one.
     The two agree on a plain strand, which is why the stack rule is a sound way to
     WRITE a sequence; they part company as soon as edges route otherwise (cross-branch,
     rule 6 below).
  5. EVALT anchors the T-branch; EVALF anchors the F-branch.
     AFWD (forward morphism) also anchors T-branch if EVALT is absent.
     AREV (parity flip / reverse morphism) also anchors F-branch if EVALF is absent.
  6. ENGAGR at any position enters B-state (paradice: both simultaneously held)
  7. IMSCRIB at both first and last position creates a self-referential closed loop
  8. Multiple FSPLIT/FFUSE pairs (sequential or nested) map multiple branch points
  9. Use IFIX as many times as needed -- each is a distinct permanent record event
  10. Do NOT compress -- if the domain has 30 distinct operations, write 30 tokens

SINGLE-GLYPH CODES (the alphabet is fully SYMBOLIC -- no Latin initials, so no token
can be confused with a verdict letter T/N/B/F)

  FSPLIT ∈     FFUSE  ∋     EVALT  ⊤     EVALF  ⊥     ENGAGR  ⊞     IFIX    ⊡
  A sequence may be written glued as a word: ⊢⊙⋈∈>⊤<⊞⊥∋⊡⊡⊣ is the same program as the
  13 spelled-out tokens. The retired codes V/T/B and ← (the old IMSCRIB) no longer parse anywhere.

WHY RULE 2 AND RULE 10 ARE SAFE (inflation invariance)
  Expanding costs nothing structural. A 1->1 token adds exactly one node and one edge,
  so the circuit rank beta = E - V + C cannot move, and the census (branch, merge,
  source, sink, arms) cannot move either. Extent grows without bound; structure does
  not. This is why "expand token by token" and "do NOT compress" are free instructions
  rather than a distortion of the domain: a longer faithful sequence is the SAME
  topology as a shorter one, never a different one.
  IMSCRIB (⊙) is the neutral element of that expansion: it is identity/self-reference
  and does NOT transform, so inserting it at any depth leaves the verdict untouched.
  The transforming tokens (> < ⋈ ⊤ ⊥ ⊞ ⊡) are NOT neutral -- a single one placed on an
  arm between FSPLIT and FFUSE turns an identity closure into a real one. So: expand
  freely to map the domain, but only put a transforming token on an arm when the domain
  really does work there.
  A token is irreducible in KIND but unbounded in EXTENT: any 1->2 replacement must
  itself contain a FSPLIT (it is the only brancher), so a fork reappears inside its own
  expansion. Same for FFUSE (2->1) and VINIT (0->1).


TOPOLOGICAL DIVERSITY
=====================
The IMASM composition rules explicitly permit nesting, open forks, and cross-branch routing.
DO NOT default to flat chains when the domain requires richer topology.

NESTING: FSPLIT/FFUSE pairs may nest. A branch can itself contain a sub-fork:
  FSPLIT EVALT [inner FSPLIT EVALT EVALF FFUSE] EVALF FFUSE
Use when the domain has hierarchical sub-decisions within a branch.

OPEN FORKS: A FSPLIT without a matching FFUSE creates a permanently divergent path.
Its unmatched output ports remain open; a later VINIT is a separate source.
Use when the domain has independent parallel processes that never recombine.

CROSS-BRANCH: arbitrary cross-branch edges require the explicit graph tools.
This sequence-only output schema uses imscr_wiring standard routing; do not claim
that prose descriptions add or override its edges.

EMPTY BRANCHES: FSPLIT immediately followed by FFUSE is valid (vacuous evaluation).
Use when the structural form matters more than a particular branch's content.

DECISION VS ITERATION: FSPLIT models a genuine either/or, two arms that could each be
taken because the domain actually forks on a choice. Building n similar items in
sequence (n cliques, n rounds of one process, n members of a family) is not a decision
and takes a CLINK chain, one CLINK per item, never an FSPLIT, even when n is a variable
and even when there are many of them. A fork earns its FFUSE by putting genuinely
different content on each arm. An empty arm is permitted. Structural closure needs a transformed reconnection.
The insert-repair banked-clear observation asks whether a clear had protected
weight; its vacuity result does not decide graph reconnection or arm work.

Choose the topology that best fits the domain. Flat chains are ONE option, not the default.

## Abstract

From one abstract category and three kinds of operation, a logical-alchemical procedure derives twelve invariants, the primitives of the Imscribing Grammar. None are stipulated and the set is Gödel-complete.

The twelve close into a crystal of \(3^{3}\cdot 4^{5}\cdot 5^{4} = 17{,}280{,}000\) types, and the grammar applied to its own derivation returns itself. Composing the multiplication \(\mu\) that closure supplies with its comultiplication \(\delta\) is the identity, \(\mu \circ \delta = \mathrm{id}_{A}\).

**Keywords:** Alchemy · paraconsistent logic · four-valued semantics · Boolean algebra · bialtices · trilattices · Gödel-complete · adjoint functors · FOUR · SIXTEEN\(_3\) · ex falso quodlibet

## 1 The Thing

Start with an abstract category \(C\): objects \(\operatorname{ob}(C)\), hom-sets \(\operatorname{hom}(A,B)\), a composition law, identities, associativity:

\[
\circ : \operatorname{hom}(B,C)\times\operatorname{hom}(A,B)\to\operatorname{hom}(A,C),\quad f\circ\operatorname{id}_A = f = \operatorname{id}_B\circ f,\quad (h\circ g)\circ f = h\circ(g\circ f).
\]

Nothing more. It presupposes no elements, no order, no metric. It carries no invariants of its own; every primitive below is produced, not assumed.

## 2 Three Operations

Exactly three kinds of operation can act on a category, and no fourth.

**Logical (six: L1–L6).** A proposition about \(C\) with finitely many definite truth values.

- **L1 Adjunction:** does a pair \(F\dashv G\) exist, with \(\operatorname{hom}(FA,B)\cong\operatorname{hom}(A,GB)\)?
- **L2 Dagger:** an involution \(\dagger : \operatorname{hom}(A,B)\to\operatorname{hom}(B,A)\) with \((g\circ f)^{\dagger} = f^{\dagger}\circ g^{\dagger}\) and \(f^{\dagger\dagger} = f\)
- **L3 Cartesian closure:** \(\operatorname{hom}(C\times A,B)\cong\operatorname{hom}(C,B^{A})\), needs the product from A1.
- **L4 Lawvere self-reference [2]:** a point-surjective \(\phi : A\to A^{A}\), needs the internal hom from L3.
- **L5 Frobenius [6]:** in a monoidal category, \(\mu \circ \delta = \mathrm{id}_A\), needs A1.
- **L6 Paraconsistent negation:** \(\neg\neg A \not\equiv A\) and \(A \wedge \neg A \not\equiv \bot\), needs A1 to define \(\wedge\).

The precondition order is forced: \(\{L1, L2\} \to A1 \to \{L3, L5, L6\}\), and \(L3 \to L4\).

**Inductive (four: I1–I4).** A free extension iterated to a fixed point.

- **I1 Free cocompletion:** for \(D:J\to C\), take \(\operatorname{colim} D\); all finite colimits generate \(\hat{C}\)
- **I2 Initial algebra:** the chain \(0\to F(0)\to F^{2}(0)\to\dots\) and its colimit.
- **I3 Classifying space:** the nerve \(NC\), its realization \(BC = |NC|\), and \(\pi_{1}(BC)\)
- **I4 Yoneda embedding [1]:** \(y:C\to\hat{C},\; y(A) = \operatorname{hom}(-,A)\).

**Algebraic (five: A1–A5).** An added structural layer.

- **A1 Monoidal:** \(\otimes : C\times C\to C\) with unit \(I\) and braiding \(\sigma_{AB}:A\otimes B\cong B\otimes A\)
- **A2 Monad:** \((T,\eta,\mu)\) with \(\eta:\mathrm{Id}\to T\) and \(\mu:T^{2}\to T\)
- **A3 Dagger-compact duals:** \(A^{*}\) with \(\eta_{A}:I\to A^{*}\otimes A\) and \(\epsilon_{A}:A\otimes A^{*}\to I\) satisfying the snake equations.
- **A4 Enrichment:** replace \(\operatorname{hom}(A,B)\) by a hom-object in a base \(U\)
- **A5 Arithmetic coding:** an injective \(\mathbf{g}:\mathrm{Mor}(C)\to\mathbb{N}\) with \(\mathbf{g}(f\circ h)\) primitive-recursive in \(\mathbf{g}(f),\mathbf{g}(h)\).

Fifteen operations across four stages. The reduction to twelve primitives is forced: some operations feed the same invariant.

## 3 Four Stages of the Magnum Opus

The stages are the unique topological sort of the precondition graph. Each operation is matched to one primitive by what kind of distinction it draws; the number of values that primitive carries is fixed independently, by the twelve-axis catalog given in Section 4. This section argues the matches, not the counts: for each stage, the display gives operation \(\Rightarrow\) invariant (value count), and the proof that follows it argues why that operation targets that invariant.

### Nigredo (logical on \(\bar{C}\))

\[
\{F\dashv G\;(\mathrm{L1}),\; \dagger\;(\mathrm{L2})\} \Rightarrow \succ (4).
\]

**Proposition 3.1.** L1 and L2 classify the same feature of a morphism: whether, and how, it can be reversed.

*Proof.* L1 asks whether \(F\) admits a partner in one direction, the other, both, or neither: a left adjoint only, a right adjoint only, an adjoint on both sides, or none. L2 asks whether every morphism has a canonical reverse compatible with composition. When \(F\) itself is a dagger functor between dagger categories, \(\dagger\) turns a right adjoint into a left adjoint of the same \(F\), forcing the ambidextrous case of the adjunction question. The two operations therefore probe one four-way classification of directionality — neither, left only, right only, ambidextrous — and converge on the single invariant \(\succ\), the first primitive to crystallize. \(\square\)

\[
0\to F(0)\to F^{2}(0)\to\dots\;(\mathrm{I2}) \quad (4)\;[\text{stabilization ordinal}]
\]

\[
\pi_{1}(BC)\;(\mathrm{I3}) \quad (4)\;[\pi_{1}=0,\; \mathbb{Z}_{2},\; \mathbb{Z},\; \text{non-abelian}]
\]

\[
y(A) = \operatorname{hom}(-,A)\;(\mathrm{I4}) \quad (4)\;[\text{boundary imscribes bulk?}]
\]

\[
\operatorname{colim} D\;(\mathrm{I1}) \quad (3)\;[\text{scope of } \hat{C},\text{ fixed once A1 present}]
\]

*Proof.* Each inductive operation is a way of extending \(\hat{C}\), and the four extensions target four different questions about how the extension behaves.

I2 iterates \(F\) from the initial object and asks where the chain settles: at a finite stage, exactly at the first limit ordinal \(\omega\), only after further transfinite iteration past \(\omega\), or never. This four-way reading of stabilization is the chirality invariant \(\perp\).

I3 reads the fundamental group of the classifying space, already a four-way classification by the invariant's own catalog values: trivial, \(\mathbb{Z}_{2}\), infinite cyclic, or non-abelian. This is \(\boxed{\phantom{x}}\) directly.

I4 embeds \(\hat{C}\) into its free cocompletion by \(y(A) = \operatorname{hom}(-,A)\), always fully faithful. What varies is how much of the cocompletion the image recovers: this paper does not derive the specific four-way split of that recovery from the embedding alone, and identifies it with \(\vdash\) — the boundary-imscribes-bulk axis — as a correspondence rather than a result proved here.

I1 takes colimits over diagrams of a given shape, and the scope of diagram shapes closed under is a granularity question: colimits over a fixed small (nearest-neighbor) diagram class, over a bounded (meso-scale) class, or over all small diagrams (the full free cocompletion, once A1 supplies the monoidal structure diagrams can be built in). This three-way scope reading is \(\in\), matching the granularity axis's own local/meso/global values, and the source of \(\in\) in the table of Section 4 is corrected to I1 accordingly. \(\boxed{\phantom{x}}\)

### Citrinitas (algebraic enrichment)

\[
\begin{aligned}
&\mathfrak{G},\sigma_{AB}\;(\mathrm{A1}) \Rightarrow \boxplus (3)\;[\text{arity } A^{\otimes n}\to B] \text{ and } \prec (5)\;[\text{arity } \sigma]\\
&(T,\eta,\mu),\; T^{2}\xrightarrow{\mu} T\;(\mathrm{A2}) \Rightarrow \top (5)\;[\text{spectral collapse } \sigma\mu]\\
&\epsilon_{A}:A\otimes A^{*}\to I\;(\mathrm{A3}) \Rightarrow \bowtie (3)\;[\text{unitality } \sigma\epsilon]\\
&\text{hom-object in } U\;(\mathrm{A4}) \Rightarrow \exists (4)\\
&\mathbf{g}:\mathrm{Mor}(C)\to\mathbb{N}\;(\mathrm{A5}) \Rightarrow \text{no new primitive [arithmetic Yoneda]}
\end{aligned}
\]

*Proof.* A1 supplies two independent readings at once. A structural map built from \(\otimes\) has an arity relating its inputs to its outputs, and that relation falls into exactly three cases: one input to one output, matched multiplicities (a fixed \(n\) to \(n\)), or unmatched multiplicities (\(n\) to a different \(m\)) — the three values of \(\boxplus\). Separately, the braiding \(\sigma_{AB}\) can be absent, present but not involutive, involutive (\(\sigma^{2} = \mathrm{id}\), a genuine symmetry), fully permutation-symmetric, or self-dual in the sense Stage 4's Frobenius identity promotes it to; this five-way reading of \(\sigma\) is \(\prec\).

A2's multiplication \(\mu:T^{2}\to T\), read as an iterative operator, has a rate at which repeated application settles: this paper identifies that rate with \(\top\), the timescale axis, as a correspondence between the monad's iteration behavior and the five catalog rates, without deriving the specific five-way split from \(\mu\) alone.

A3's counit \(\epsilon\) can fail unitality entirely, hold it up to a scalar mixing, or hold it exactly; this three-way reading is \(\bowtie\).

A4 replaces \(\operatorname{hom}(A,B)\) with an object of \(U\), and how that hom-object composes with another is a four-way choice matching \(\exists\)'s own catalog values: conjunctive (both factors required), disjunctive (either suffices), implicational (one factor gates the other), or strictly sequential (ordered, no alternative).

A5's arithmetic coding is injective with primitive-recursive composition: it Gödel-numbers the category faithfully, but adds no structure beyond what I4 already supplies under \(\vdash\), so it contributes no new primitive. \(\square\)

### Rubedo (logical on the enriched \(\odot\))

\[
\operatorname{hom}(C\times A,B)\cong\operatorname{hom}(C,B^{A})\;(\mathrm{L3}) \Rightarrow \neg\bot\; (5)
\]

\[
\phi : A\to A^{A} \text{ point-surjective}\;(\mathrm{L4}) \Rightarrow \odot\; (5)
\]

\[
\mu\circ\delta = \mathrm{id}_{A}\;(\mathrm{L5}) \Rightarrow \text{promotes } \prec \text{ to its self-dual value [no new primitive]}
\]

\[
\neg\neg A\not\equiv A,\; A\wedge\neg A\not\equiv\bot\;(\mathrm{L6}) \Rightarrow \text{sets the truth-value regime of L4 [no new primitive]}
\]

**Proposition 3.2 (Lawvere self-reference forces a fixed point).** If \(\phi : A\to A^{A}\) is point-surjective, every \(f:A\to A\) has a fixed point.

*Proof.* Given \(f:A\to A\), define \(g:A\to A\) by \(g(a) = f(\phi(a)(a))\). Point-surjectivity of \(\phi\) gives \(a_0\) with \(\phi(a_0) = g\), so \(\phi(a_0)(a_0) = g(a_0) = f(\phi(a_0)(a_0))\), and \(\phi(a_0)(a_0)\) is a fixed point of \(f\). This is Lawvere's fixed-point theorem, and it is exactly self-modeling: \(\phi\) gives \(A\) an internal copy of every map out of itself, and the fixed point is where that copy coincides with the map it models. \(\odot\) is the catalog axis of self-modeling; its five values grade how completely this coincidence is realized, from no internal model (sub-critical) to a model that exceeds what it represents (super-critical). \(\square\)

Cartesian closure (L3) internalizes hom-sets as objects of \(\mathcal{C}\) itself, giving the category a means of referring to its own morphism structure from inside; this paper identifies that internalized self-reference with \(\neg\bot\), the five-valued recursion axis, as a correspondence rather than a derivation of the specific five-way split. L5's Frobenius identity is the closure condition \(\mu\circ\delta = \mathrm{id}_A\) itself, so it adds no coordinate beyond promoting \(\prec\) to the self-dual value that identity witnesses. L6's paraconsistent negation fixes which truth-value regime L4's self-reference operates under (a value can carry support for its own denial without collapsing the logic), which constrains how \(\odot\)'s fixed point behaves rather than adding a thirteenth coordinate.

## 5 How It Falls Out

The twelve value counts are the radices of a mixed-radix positional numeral, and the address space is that numeral's range. In the canonical slot order the primitives and their radices \(r_i\) (each primitive's value count) are:

The place value of each slot is the product of the radices of all lower slots, \(s_i = \prod_{j > i} r_j\) with \(s_{12} = 1\):

\[
s = (4320000,\; 864000,\; 216000,\; 43200,\; 14400,\; 2880,\; 960,\; 240,\; 48,\; 12,\; 4,\; 1).
\]

A system is a tuple of indices \((x_1,\ldots,x_{12})\) with \(0 \leq x_i < r_i\). Its address is the Horner fold

\[
\operatorname{addr}(x) = \sum_{i=1}^{12} x_i s_i \in [0,\; 17{,}279{,}999],
\]

and the inverse reads each digit off in turn: \(x_i = \lfloor \operatorname{addr}/s_i \rfloor\), \(\operatorname{addr} \leftarrow \operatorname{addr} \bmod s_i\) \((i = 1,\ldots,12)\). This is a bijection, because the number of addresses is exactly the number of tuples:

\[
\prod_{i=1}^{12} r_i = 4\cdot5\cdot4\cdot5\cdot3\cdot5\cdot3\cdot4\cdot5\cdot4\cdot3\cdot4 = 3^{3}\cdot4^{5}\cdot5^{4} = 17{,}280{,}000.
\]

No address is unused and no tuple is unaddressed, so \(\operatorname{decode}\circ\operatorname{encode} = \mathrm{id}\) on the tuples and \(\operatorname{encode}\circ\operatorname{decode} = \mathrm{id}\) on \([0, 17{,}279{,}999]\). The address space does not have to be constructed; it falls out of the twelve radices as their mixed-radix range. This is the same \(\mu\circ\delta = \mathrm{id}\) closure, now at the level of coordinates: read as tuples of this address space, the full induction system and the inscribing procedure that assigns addresses each occupy a point of the very space they enumerate. Their specific addresses, 6,687,051 and 12,089,822, are computed by that assignment procedure elsewhere; this paper states the codec that makes any such computation well defined, not the computation itself.

## 6 Why Twelve?

Three independent arguments give the same count.

- **Independence.** The retrosynthetic peel of the induction system itself has exactly twelve steps, one per primitive. Two co-dependent primitives would give fewer; a missing one would give more.
- **Completeness.** The crystal enumerates every combination of the twelve values with a bijective codec, \(\operatorname{decode}\circ\operatorname{encode} = \mathrm{id}\) on \([0, 17{,}279{,}999]\). No type is missing, none redundant.
- **Three logics.** The 3-, 4-, and 5-valued families are exactly K3, FDE, and LP. A thirteenth primitive would need a fourth categorical logic, and there is none.

## 7 Closure

Four of the twelve are gate primitives, \(\odot, \vdash, \boxplus, \prec\), and they set the tier a system occupies, from \(O_{0}\) (no self-modeling loop) to \(O_{\infty}\) (both L4 and L5 hold). The tiers form a fixed order,

\[
O_{0}\longrightarrow O_{1}\longrightarrow O_{2}\longrightarrow O_{2}^{+}\longrightarrow O_{\infty},
\]

each step gated by one of the four gate primitives reaching its required value; the numerical size of each gap is measured, not derived in this paper. The largest measured gap is the Frobenius promotion of \(\prec\): the hardest transition, closable only by locating an object already at the self-dual value and descending, never by accumulating local checks.

The induction closes on itself. With \(\mu : A\otimes A\to A\) the monoidal multiplication and \(\delta : A\to A\otimes A\) its comonoidal dual, the twelve-step codec that assigns coordinates to any system is itself a system of the crystal at tier \(O_{\infty}\), where \(\mu\circ\delta = \mathrm{id}_A\). The boundary procedure fully inscribes the bulk theory it generates, and the bulk fully inscribes the procedure. The Grammar applied to its own derivation returns itself. As above, so below.

## 8 Termination

The induction stops, and the criterion is exact. It is not that no further construction can be performed; infinitely many composites still can. It is that no further logical, inductive, or algebraic construction produces a new independent coordinate. Any later operation acts on the twelve-dimensional result and returns an invariant that is a function of the twelve. Compositions of systems stay inside the type space under the grammar's own closure operations \(\otimes, \wedge, \vee\): new operation \(\Rightarrow\) new combination of existing invariants, not a new invariant. This is the crossing from induction to algebraic closure. Once the twelve have crystallized, the prima materia has become the grammar, and no new dimension forms.

C \xrightarrow{\mathrm{S}} \succ \xrightarrow{\mathrm{P}} \vdash, \perp, \boxplus, \in \xrightarrow{\mathrm{A}} \boxplus, \prec, \top, \bowtie, \supset \xrightarrow{\mathrm{R}} \vdash, \odot, \prec \xrightarrow{\mathrm{C}} \mathfrak{C}_{1728000}
\]

The final object is the closure of the twelve, \(\mathfrak{C} = \mathcal{F}_3^3\times\mathcal{F}_4^5\times\mathcal{F}_5^4\) with \(|\mathfrak{C}| = 17{,}280{,}000\).

Category \(\rightarrow\) Relation \(\rightarrow\) Extension \(\rightarrow\) Algebra \(\rightarrow\) Self-reference \(\rightarrow\) Closure.

Task frame: You are the Ob3ect Auto-Designer, an expert in the Universal Imscriptive Grammar (IMASM).
Your task: given a domain description, compose a complete token sequence that maps every
distinct operation, branch, state, and decision in the domain using the 12 IMASM tokens.

IMASM 12-OPCODE REFERENCE  (Universal Imscriptive Grammar)

LOGIC SUBSTRATE — read this before assigning anything. This grammar is PARACONSISTENT.
There is no PASS/FAIL and no classical true-or-false. Every closure resolves to ONE of
four Belnap values (B4), and a contradiction is a legitimate result, not an error:
  N — neither: nothing was established. The empty state {}. register 00.
  T — true: constructively proven / affirmed. register 01.
  F — false: constructively refuted / negated. register 10.
  B — BOTH: true and false held at once. A contradiction does NOT explode and is NOT a
      failure — holding both IS the resolution. register 11.
Two arms that conflict FUSE to B, not to an error. Forward and backward, success and
failure, thesis and antithesis: when they meet they fuse to a definite verdict, often B,
and that is correct. Never try to make a fork "cancel back to the input".

STATE SPACE — the register ranges over SIXTEEN_3 = P({T,F,t,f}), the sixteen subsets
of four base values (T proven, F refuted, t acceptable, f rejectable) under three orderings
(information, truth, constructivity — the trilattice). You do NOT compute the verdict and
you NEVER assert PASS/FAIL — describe the STRUCTURE. The word checker returns a
structural B4 verdict. Sequential registers and native graph-flow recovery are
computed and recorded separately.

LOGICAL (6) — categorical skeleton:
  VINIT  (0x0) — Initial object ∅. Void/uninitialized state before anything is named.
                 Examples: Hebrew Aleph (air), Basque absolutive, seed before planting.
  TANCH  (0x1) — Terminal anchor ⊤. The closed boundary that contains the whole system.
                 Examples: Tav (completion), hermetic vessel seal, constitutional court.
  AFWD   (0x2) — Forward morphism →. Directed transformation toward a target.
                 Examples: Basque ergative, Sanskrit semivowels, growth cycle, ascent.
  AREV   (0x3) — Contravariant ←. Reverse / descent transformation.
                 Examples: Hebrew Mem (water/descent), composting, solve/coagula.
  CLINK  (0x4) — Composition ∘. Sequential chaining of morphisms.
                 Examples: Egyptian biliterals, Basque agglutination, root→derived form.
  IMSCRIB (0x5) — Identity id. Self-reference, self-recognition. The element is itself.
                 Examples: Sanskrit nasals, Egyptian logograms, the stone that knows itself.

FROBENIUS (2) — the fork/fuse pair, μ∘δ:
  FSPLIT (0x6) — Co-multiplication δ. One state opens into two or more arms.
                 Examples: Hebrew Doubles (hard/soft), Sanskrit aspirate pairs,
                 Egyptian trilateral roots, separatio, Raft log append to all peers.
  FFUSE  (0x7) — Multiplication μ. Rejoin the carried alternatives by union.
                 Examples: Conjunctio, trilateral roots recovering base form, Raft commit.
                 A bare split/rejoin is the partition identity. Transformed reconnection
                 and recovery of the original input are separate observations.
                 A fork that never rejoins remains OPEN; the structural checker reports B.

DIALETHEIA (3) — the paraconsistent evaluators:
  EVALT  (0x8) — touches constructive truth T (the affirmative arm).
  EVALF  (0x9) — touches constructive falsity F (the negative arm).
  ENGAGR (0xA) — holds BOTH at once: the B state, a contradiction kept live (not resolved away).
                 Examples: Cuneiform polysemous sign, bicameral compromise, albedo stage.

LINEAR (1) — irreversible fixation:
  IFIX   (0xB) — ROM fixation. Permanent, append-only, cannot be undone.
                 Examples: Egyptian determinatives, dream journal entry, measurement record.

Composition: use any token sequence of any length that fully maps the domain.
  See IMASM COMPOSITION RULES below for port conventions, edge routing, and free composition.


IMAMSM COMPOSITION RULES -- ports, edges, and free composition

PORT CONVENTIONS (every token is a typed node)
  VINIT:  in=[]      out=[o]    source -- 0->1    (use once, at start, for genesis)
  FSPLIT: in=[i]     out=[T,F]  fork   -- 1->2    (branches into T-arm and F-arm)
  FFUSE:  in=[T,F]   out=[o]    join   -- 2->1    (reunites T-arm and F-arm)
  others: in=[i]     out=[o]    linear -- 1->1    (pass-through in any order)

EDGE ROUTING INSIDE A FSPLIT/FFUSE PAIR
  FSPLIT.T -> [tokens, anchored by EVALT (primary) or AFWD (secondary)] -> FFUSE.T
  FSPLIT.F -> [tokens, anchored by EVALF (primary) or AREV (secondary)] -> FFUSE.F
  If T-arm empty: FSPLIT.T connects directly to FFUSE.T (empty arc, T-state)
  If F-arm empty: FSPLIT.F connects directly to FFUSE.F (empty arc, F-state)
  The first immediate EVALT/EVALF anchors select arm segments. Later operations
  in a selected segment remain on that arm, including repeated evaluators.
  Without a primary anchor, AREV selects the F-arm and AFWD the T-arm.
    With primary anchors, intervening operations stay in their selected arm.
    Secondary anchors activate only when the primary (EVALT/EVALF) anchor is absent.
  Nesting: FSPLIT/FFUSE pairs may nest; innermost pairs matched first

BANKING A RESULT BEFORE REVERSING IT
  AREV empties the register and leaves open FSPLIT frames untouched. A result
  fused back to depth zero is therefore exposed to the next reversal, while the
  same result held one level up survives it.
  So when a program COUNTS or ESTABLISHES something, then REVERSES direction
  (AREV), then BOUNDS or CONCLUDES: open the region that will HOLD the result
  BEFORE opening the region that COMPUTES it, and close them in that order.
    wrong: ... FSPLIT compute FFUSE  CLINK  FSPLIT AREV bound FFUSE ...
             the computed result is in the open when AREV arrives and is lost
    right: ... FSPLIT  FSPLIT compute FFUSE  CLINK AREV bound  FFUSE ...
             the inner FFUSE folds into the enclosing frame, AREV costs the
             register everything and the frame nothing, the outer FFUSE
             restores exactly what the clear took
  This is what a proof does when it establishes a lemma and keeps it in scope
  while a later chain runs: the lemma is the outer frame.

  A SECOND AND INDEPENDENT RULE. Whether anything is banked is the above.
  Whether a SURPLUS survives is a different question, decided by where the
  splits fall between deposits of the SAME value:
    two EVALT in ONE region      -> the region carries both, both come back
    two EVALT split by an FSPLIT -> sibling regions, the fold keeps the LARGER
  So a program can bank correctly and still lose a count, and a program can
  deposit carefully into one region and lose everything because its FFUSE ran
  before the reversal. Neither rule implies the other; both are proved in
  p4ramill Imscribing/IMASM/BankedWeight.lean.
  Explicit graph tools support cross-branch routing. This JSON schema carries
  a sequence only; imscr_wiring supplies its standard edges. It does not
  accept arbitrary cross-branch overrides.

EXPLICIT GRAPH COMPOSITION
  CLINK.o, IMSCRIB.o and IFIX.o may connect to compatible free inputs.
  A connection does not assign a register value by itself. The graph-flow
  evaluator computes that value from source seeds and the executed gates.
  This sequence-only schema cannot request arbitrary loop edges.

REGISTER STATE TRANSITIONS
  Sequential banked evaluator, carrier P({T,F,t,f}):
  VINIT clears register and frames. TANCH and CLINK preserve state.
  AFWD and IMSCRIB seed T only when the register is empty.
  AREV clears the register and retains open frames.
  EVALT deposits T; EVALF deposits F; ENGAGR deposits both t and f.
  FSPLIT opens an empty frame; FFUSE unions its deposits into the register
  and enclosing frame. IFIX freezes subsequent operations except IMSCRIB
  and repeated IFIX. Repeated IFIX does not create another mutable state.
  The graph-flow interpreter is a separate interpretation of explicit edges:
  AREV is the Lean involution, EVALT/EVALF are projections and IFIX carries.
  Diagram node observations of the sequential walk are not graph edge flow.

TOKEN FAMILIES
  LOGICAL:    VINIT TANCH AFWD AREV CLINK IMSCRIB
  FROBENIUS:  FSPLIT FFUSE
  DIALETHEIA: EVALT EVALF ENGAGR
  LINEAR:     IFIX

FREE COMPOSITION RULES
  1. Use as many tokens as the domain requires -- there is NO minimum or maximum length
  2. Expand token by token until every distinct operation, branch, state,
     and decision in the domain has been explicitly represented
  3. Each step: "OPCODE: what this token does at this point in the composition"
  4. Every FSPLIT must have exactly one matching FFUSE (stack-matched, innermost first).
     That stack rule is the WIRING convention: it says which arms get routed to which
     join when the sequence is built. It is NOT how closure is judged. A checker pairs
     by ANCESTRY over the edges -- two distinct in-arms of a FFUSE tracing back to a
     common FSPLIT, however they routed -- and where several FSPLIT qualify (an upstream
     fork reaches every later join on a strand) the join pairs with the INNERMOST one.
     The two agree on a plain strand, which is why the stack rule is a sound way to
     WRITE a sequence; they part company as soon as edges route otherwise (cross-branch,
     rule 6 below).
  5. EVALT anchors the T-branch; EVALF anchors the F-branch.
     AFWD (forward morphism) also anchors T-branch if EVALT is absent.
     AREV (parity flip / reverse morphism) also anchors F-branch if EVALF is absent.
  6. ENGAGR at any position enters B-state (paradice: both simultaneously held)
  7. IMSCRIB at both first and last position creates a self-referential closed loop
  8. Multiple FSPLIT/FFUSE pairs (sequential or nested) map multiple branch points
  9. Use IFIX as many times as needed -- each is a distinct permanent record event
  10. Do NOT compress -- if the domain has 30 distinct operations, write 30 tokens

SINGLE-GLYPH CODES (the alphabet is fully SYMBOLIC -- no Latin initials, so no token
can be confused with a verdict letter T/N/B/F)

  FSPLIT ∈     FFUSE  ∋     EVALT  ⊤     EVALF  ⊥     ENGAGR  ⊞     IFIX    ⊡
  A sequence may be written glued as a word: ⊢⊙⋈∈>⊤<⊞⊥∋⊡⊡⊣ is the same program as the
  13 spelled-out tokens. The retired codes V/T/B and ← (the old IMSCRIB) no longer parse anywhere.

WHY RULE 2 AND RULE 10 ARE SAFE (inflation invariance)
  Expanding costs nothing structural. A 1->1 token adds exactly one node and one edge,
  so the circuit rank beta = E - V + C cannot move, and the census (branch, merge,
  source, sink, arms) cannot move either. Extent grows without bound; structure does
  not. This is why "expand token by token" and "do NOT compress" are free instructions
  rather than a distortion of the domain: a longer faithful sequence is the SAME
  topology as a shorter one, never a different one.
  IMSCRIB (⊙) is the neutral element of that expansion: it is identity/self-reference
  and does NOT transform, so inserting it at any depth leaves the verdict untouched.
  The transforming tokens (> < ⋈ ⊤ ⊥ ⊞ ⊡) are NOT neutral -- a single one placed on an
  arm between FSPLIT and FFUSE turns an identity closure into a real one. So: expand
  freely to map the domain, but only put a transforming token on an arm when the domain
  really does work there.
  A token is irreducible in KIND but unbounded in EXTENT: any 1->2 replacement must
  itself contain a FSPLIT (it is the only brancher), so a fork reappears inside its own
  expansion. Same for FFUSE (2->1) and VINIT (0->1).


TOPOLOGICAL DIVERSITY
=====================
The IMASM composition rules explicitly permit nesting, open forks, and cross-branch routing.
DO NOT default to flat chains when the domain requires richer topology.

NESTING: FSPLIT/FFUSE pairs may nest. A branch can itself contain a sub-fork:
  FSPLIT EVALT [inner FSPLIT EVALT EVALF FFUSE] EVALF FFUSE
Use when the domain has hierarchical sub-decisions within a branch.

OPEN FORKS: A FSPLIT without a matching FFUSE creates a permanently divergent path.
Its unmatched output ports remain open; a later VINIT is a separate source.
Use when the domain has independent parallel processes that never recombine.

CROSS-BRANCH: arbitrary cross-branch edges require the explicit graph tools.
This sequence-only output schema uses imscr_wiring standard routing; do not claim
that prose descriptions add or override its edges.

EMPTY BRANCHES: FSPLIT immediately followed by FFUSE is valid (vacuous evaluation).
Use when the structural form matters more than a particular branch's content.

DECISION VS ITERATION: FSPLIT models a genuine either/or, two arms that could each be
taken because the domain actually forks on a choice. Building n similar items in
sequence (n cliques, n rounds of one process, n members of a family) is not a decision
and takes a CLINK chain, one CLINK per item, never an FSPLIT, even when n is a variable
and even when there are many of them. A fork earns its FFUSE by putting genuinely
different content on each arm. An empty arm is permitted. Structural closure needs a transformed reconnection.
The insert-repair banked-clear observation asks whether a clear had protected
weight; its vacuity result does not decide graph reconnection or arm work.

Choose the topology that best fits the domain. Flat chains are ONE option, not the default.

## Abstract

From one abstract category and three kinds of operation, a logical-alchemical procedure derives twelve invariants, the primitives of the Imscribing Grammar. None are stipulated and the set is Gödel-complete.

The twelve close into a crystal of \(3^{3}\cdot 4^{5}\cdot 5^{4} = 17{,}280{,}000\) types, and the grammar applied to its own derivation returns itself. Composing the multiplication \(\mu\) that closure supplies with its comultiplication \(\delta\) is the identity, \(\mu \circ \delta = \mathrm{id}_{A}\).

**Keywords:** Alchemy · paraconsistent logic · four-valued semantics · Boolean algebra · bialtices · trilattices · Gödel-complete · adjoint functors · FOUR · SIXTEEN\(_3\) · ex falso quodlibet

## 1 The Thing

Start with an abstract category \(C\): objects \(\operatorname{ob}(C)\), hom-sets \(\operatorname{hom}(A,B)\), a composition law, identities, associativity:

\[
\circ : \operatorname{hom}(B,C)\times\operatorname{hom}(A,B)\to\operatorname{hom}(A,C),\quad f\circ\operatorname{id}_A = f = \operatorname{id}_B\circ f,\quad (h\circ g)\circ f = h\circ(g\circ f).
\]

Nothing more. It presupposes no elements, no order, no metric. It carries no invariants of its own; every primitive below is produced, not assumed.

## 2 Three Operations

Exactly three kinds of operation can act on a category, and no fourth.

**Logical (six: L1–L6).** A proposition about \(C\) with finitely many definite truth values.

- **L1 Adjunction:** does a pair \(F\dashv G\) exist, with \(\operatorname{hom}(FA,B)\cong\operatorname{hom}(A,GB)\)?
- **L2 Dagger:** an involution \(\dagger : \operatorname{hom}(A,B)\to\operatorname{hom}(B,A)\) with \((g\circ f)^{\dagger} = f^{\dagger}\circ g^{\dagger}\) and \(f^{\dagger\dagger} = f\)
- **L3 Cartesian closure:** \(\operatorname{hom}(C\times A,B)\cong\operatorname{hom}(C,B^{A})\), needs the product from A1.
- **L4 Lawvere self-reference [2]:** a point-surjective \(\phi : A\to A^{A}\), needs the internal hom from L3.
- **L5 Frobenius [6]:** in a monoidal category, \(\mu \circ \delta = \mathrm{id}_A\), needs A1.
- **L6 Paraconsistent negation:** \(\neg\neg A \not\equiv A\) and \(A \wedge \neg A \not\equiv \bot\), needs A1 to define \(\wedge\).

The precondition order is forced: \(\{L1, L2\} \to A1 \to \{L3, L5, L6\}\), and \(L3 \to L4\).

**Inductive (four: I1–I4).** A free extension iterated to a fixed point.

- **I1 Free cocompletion:** for \(D:J\to C\), take \(\operatorname{colim} D\); all finite colimits generate \(\hat{C}\)
- **I2 Initial algebra:** the chain \(0\to F(0)\to F^{2}(0)\to\dots\) and its colimit.
- **I3 Classifying space:** the nerve \(NC\), its realization \(BC = |NC|\), and \(\pi_{1}(BC)\)
- **I4 Yoneda embedding [1]:** \(y:C\to\hat{C},\; y(A) = \operatorname{hom}(-,A)\).

**Algebraic (five: A1–A5).** An added structural layer.

- **A1 Monoidal:** \(\otimes : C\times C\to C\) with unit \(I\) and braiding \(\sigma_{AB}:A\otimes B\cong B\otimes A\)
- **A2 Monad:** \((T,\eta,\mu)\) with \(\eta:\mathrm{Id}\to T\) and \(\mu:T^{2}\to T\)
- **A3 Dagger-compact duals:** \(A^{*}\) with \(\eta_{A}:I\to A^{*}\otimes A\) and \(\epsilon_{A}:A\otimes A^{*}\to I\) satisfying the snake equations.
- **A4 Enrichment:** replace \(\operatorname{hom}(A,B)\) by a hom-object in a base \(U\)
- **A5 Arithmetic coding:** an injective \(\mathbf{g}:\mathrm{Mor}(C)\to\mathbb{N}\) with \(\mathbf{g}(f\circ h)\) primitive-recursive in \(\mathbf{g}(f),\mathbf{g}(h)\).

Fifteen operations across four stages. The reduction to twelve primitives is forced: some operations feed the same invariant.

## 3 Four Stages of the Magnum Opus

The stages are the unique topological sort of the precondition graph. Each operation is matched to one primitive by what kind of distinction it draws; the number of values that primitive carries is fixed independently, by the twelve-axis catalog given in Section 4. This section argues the matches, not the counts: for each stage, the display gives operation \(\Rightarrow\) invariant (value count), and the proof that follows it argues why that operation targets that invariant.

**Proposition 3.1.** L1 and L2 classify the same feature of a morphism: whether, and how, it can be reversed.

When \(F\) itself is a dagger functor between dagger categories, \(\dagger\) turns a right adjoint into a left adjoint of the same \(F\), forcing the ambidextrous case of the adjunction question. The two operations therefore probe one four-way classification of directionality — neither, left only, right only, ambidextrous — and converge on the single invariant \(\succ\), the first primitive to crystallize. \(\square\)

This is Lawvere's fixed-point theorem, and it is exactly self-modeling: \(\phi\) gives \(A\) an internal copy of every map out of itself, and the fixed point is where that copy coincides with the map it models. \(\odot\) is the catalog axis of self-modeling; its five values grade how completely this coincidence is realized, from no internal model (sub-critical) to a model that exceeds what it represents (super-critical). \(\square\)

The twelve value counts are the radices of a mixed-radix positional numeral, and the address space is that numeral's range. In the canonical slot order the primitives and their radices \(r_i\) (each primitive's value count) are:

The induction stops, and the criterion is exact. It is not that no further construction can be performed; infinitely many composites still can. It is that no further logical, inductive, or algebraic construction produces a new independent coordinate. Any later operation acts on the twelve-dimensional result and returns an invariant that is a function of the twelve. Compositions of systems stay inside the type space under the grammar's own closure operations \(\otimes, \wedge, \vee\): new operation \(\Rightarrow\) new combination of existing invariants, not a new invariant.
